views.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one photorealistic entrance interior image, portrait.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, Mockup 03 of the actual house. Make a precise small revision, preserving the exact composition, camera, architecture, illumination and every other item.
User feedback: tabletop is over-accessorised. They want CURATED, ELEGANT, CHIC, with calm space around a few considered objects.
Change ONLY the console tabletop:
- Remove BOTH stacked books completely.
- Remove the small oval leaning picture frame completely.
- Retain the existing small traditional brass lamp with pleated olive shade at the door end, exactly its current scale and style.
- Retain the compact aspidistra in its green glazed pot at the far end, subtly contain its spread if necessary for clear space.
- Retain exactly ONE small shallow blue-and-white porcelain key dish, resting DIRECTLY on the bare wood at centre (not on books), with a restrained amount of pattern, no keys scattered around it.
- Arrange lamp, pot and dish with generous breathing space. The curved dark wood tabletop should be clearly visible between them. Exactly three tabletop objects/groups: lamp, potted plant, small dish. No books, photo frames, ornaments, candle, vase, flowers, trays, added objects or decorative clutter. Preserve console identity and size, do not enlarge it.
LOCK EVERYTHING ELSE: the front door with exact tulip stained-glass pattern, sidelight, fanlight, exterior lantern, all original pale wall and white panelling paint, cornice, ribbed-glass pendants, brass door hardware, original intricate grey/black/ivory STAR-pattern geometric floor tiles at same scale, black steel lounge glazing on left, existing dark hammered mirror, turned walnut/brass coat stand and single olive jacket/lead, wicker hamper beneath console, coir mat, cropped white stair newel. Keep stairs bare if any are visible. Keep same narrow hall proportions.
Do not redesign room, change rug, add wall art, repaint, alter furniture, widen hall, change material colours or move any architectural elements. Keep natural photographic detail and realistic reflections. No text, labels, arrows, borders or watermarks.

steps.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one photorealistic hallway interior image, portrait.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, Mockup 03 of this actual hallway. Change ONLY the Persian-style hall runner. Preserve exact photographic framing, room geometry, paint, all other objects and lighting.
User likes Persian design but the existing dark intricate rug clashes with the sharp geometric star tiles. They want brown with a softly faded, 'blurry' pattern so it feels chic and harmonious. Interpret 'blurry' as worn, low-contrast woven motifs, NOT optical blur in the photograph.
Replace existing strong dark runner with an elegant timeworn Persian-style WOOL runner in a LIGHTER SOFT MUSHROOM / TAUPE-BROWN / PALE TOBACCO palette. It is distinctly brown-toned but mellow and softly mottled. Faint traditional Persian floral tendrils and ghosted small medallions in adjacent shades of brown, warm stone and pale camel, with at most tiny traces of dusty muted rust. VERY LOW PATTERN CONTRAST: motif about 10-15 percent different in tone from the ground. The traditional design is gently discernible up close but softly dissolves at hallway distance. Think deeply faded heirloom wool with abrash variation and erased drawing, not a brightly new beige print, plain sisal mat, modern abstract rug, block border or distressed graphic.
Border similarly faded and tonal, only one or two shades from field, NO black/charcoal/navy frame, NO bright ivory outlines or vivid red. Matte dense low-pile wool texture stays SHARP AND IN FOCUS with realistic fibres. Do not blur room, floor or photograph. The rug should complement the oak stair and pale grey walls, with much less contrast than the surrounding original geometric tiles.
Proportion and fit: about 55-60cm wide, centred in tiled walkway, continuous generous visible tile strips at both sides. Stop short of rear doorway with an obvious 12-20cm tiled threshold gap and keep entrance square uncarpeted. Slightly shorten the rug compared with input so the end/landing is clear. No tassels or long fringe; lies completely flat. Do not change the original tiles to help the rug match.
LOCK REST OF IMAGE: completely BARE OAK stair treads AND risers, white turned newel and balusters, dark handrail, exact original panelling and sloping trim, three traditional English landscape paintings in aged gilt frames ABOVE panelling with diagonal rising centres, same paintings and positions, pale grey wall paint, flush cupboards with same seams, original black/grey/ivory STAR MOSAIC tiles, black steel glazed lounge door at right, original rear door/transom, kitchen and garden sightline, cornice and ceiling fixtures. Keep narrow hall width, photographic perspective and all material detail. No stair runner, carpet on steps or rods. Do not add objects or alter artwork. No text, watermark, collage or labels.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image is the edit target. Change ONLY the rug in this hallway photograph. Everything outside the rug must remain identical: oak stairs bare, same three gilt landscape paintings above original panelling, original exact star mosaic tiles, all architecture, light and perspective.
The rug still has too much crisp detail. User explicitly wants a brown Persian design that looks blurry/faded so it does not clash with the very sharp patterned floor.
Give the rug an exceptionally worn erased heirloom appearance: roughly 75-85% of the pattern pigment faded away into the wool. Soft mushroom-brown, warm greige and dusty pale tobacco. Same overall warm brown family as now, slightly more muted and desaturated. GHOSTED Persian motifs remain only as very faint tonal traces, some patches almost completely worn away, not a neat new repeated ornamental print. From this camera distance it should read primarily as a mellow brown textile with barely legible traditional motifs. No bright ivory detail, dark brown outlines, orange field, dark frame border or strong central medallions. The border must also almost dissolve into the field. Keep real wool pile and fine fibres sharply photographed; the PATTERN has faded, not the photo blurred. No Gaussian blur on carpet, room or tile.
Also shorten the FAR END of the rug by one full floor-tile row so a clearly visible band of ORIGINAL star mosaic tile separates rug end and rear kitchen doorway. Near end and side tile margins stay as in the image; do not widen rug. Leave entire staircase bare and all wall art unchanged. Photorealistic small precise edit, nothing else added or redesigned.

views.review: The first pass remained too strongly drawn. The selected second pass further reduces pattern and border contrast and reveals a tiled threshold.

notes: Exact prompts and intermediate hallway output preserved. Outputs copied without post-processing. Previous iteration files unchanged. New edits inherit the inferred upper-wall extension from 03; geometry and objects are not dimensionally verified. Generation is nondeterministic.
